result.summary: The image shows a wide residential street with a significant lack of pedestrian infrastructure. There are no marked crosswalks, traffic control devices, or lane markings visible, creating an environment where pedestrians must cross wide expanses of asphalt without protection or priority.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks at the junction, forcing pedestrians to cross without designated space or driver warning.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the intersection of the two roads

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings and the width of the road can encourage higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway stretching from foreground to background

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The transition from the sidewalk to the street lacks ramps, creating a barrier for people with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side where the sidewalk meets the driveway/road

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to define pedestrian space and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct curb extensions (bulb-outs) to reduce crossing distance and slow turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Lane Markings
interventions.description: Add clear lane markings to organize traffic flow and narrow the perceived width of the travel lanes.

result.summary: The residential environment lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure, with no visible sidewalks or marked crosswalks. Pedestrians are forced to walk in the roadway or on unpaved surfaces, and the wide, unmarked street may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of sidewalks
hazards.description: Pedestrians have no dedicated space and must walk in the roadway or on grass.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street throughout the frame.

hazards.name: Unmarked crossing
hazards.description: No designated crossing point at the intersection increases risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflict.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide safe pedestrian separation.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks and Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Paint high-visibility crosswalks and install ADA-compliant curb ramps at the intersection.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Implement measures like curb extensions or speed humps to reduce vehicle speeds on this wide residential street.

result.summary: This residential intersection features sidewalks but lacks basic pedestrian crossing infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps. The wide, unmarked roadway and presence of parked vehicles near the corner create potential conflicts and sightline issues for people crossing the street.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection to designate a safe path for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk ends at a standard curb height without a ramp, creating a barrier for those with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk on the left

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the side street may block the view between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the curb

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Compliant Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install tactile, sloped curb ramps at all corners of the intersection to improve accessibility.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection corners to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a lack of basic safety infrastructure such as marked crosswalks or signals at the intersection. A large utility pole significantly obstructs the sidewalk at the corner, and the adjacent commercial land use with wide open access points increases potential vehicle-pedestrian conflict.

hazards.name: Utility Pole Obstruction
hazards.description: A large wooden utility pole is located directly in the center of the sidewalk corner, severely restricting pedestrian movement and accessibility.
hazards.location_in_image: Right foreground on the sidewalk corner

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at this intersection, making pedestrian crossing points unclear to drivers.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A trailer and utility pole block sight lines between pedestrians waiting to cross and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the corner

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Move the utility pole out of the pedestrian clear zone to ensure an unobstructed and ADA-compliant path.
